meaning: The way fabric falls and hangs on the body.
usage: Use it to describe how a saree looks when worn.

examples.sentence: This silk has a beautiful drape.
The cotton drapes well and is easy to pleat.

remember: Say 'a beautiful drape', not 'a beautiful fall'. Verb: 'It drapes well.'

meaning: A fold in fabric, pressed or sewn flat.
usage: Use it when you talk about wearing a saree.

examples.sentence: Make five or six pleats at the front.
The pleats stay in place all day.

remember: Spelling: PLEAT, not 'plait' (that is hair).

meaning: The decorated loose end of a saree that goes over the shoulder.
usage: Use it to describe the most detailed part.

examples.sentence: The pallu has a hand-woven gold motif.
The pallu is heavier than the body.

remember: In English, 'pallu' and 'pallav' are both used. Keep one in all your posts.

meaning: The edge design along the length of a saree.
usage: Use it to describe the design at the edges.

examples.sentence: A wide zari border in gold.
The border is contrast green.

remember: Wide border, thin border, contrast border.

meaning: Shiny gold or silver thread used in weaving.
usage: Use it for gold-coloured work in borders and pallus.

examples.sentence: Pure zari work.
The zari is soft, so it does not scratch.

remember: Say 'pure zari' only if true. 'Tested zari' or 'imitation zari' are honest alternatives.

meaning: Made on a loom by hand, not by a machine.
usage: Use it to show quality and justify price.

examples.sentence: A handwoven cotton saree from Kerala.
Each piece is handwoven, so small differences are normal.

remember: One word: handwoven. Not 'hand woven'.

meaning: How the fabric feels when touched.
usage: Use it for the feel of a fabric.

examples.sentence: The texture is soft and light.
It has a slightly crisp texture.

remember: Texture = feel. Pattern = design. Colour = shade.

meaning: Not heavy, easy to wear for long.
usage: Use it for summer and office sarees.

examples.sentence: A lightweight cotton saree for daily wear.
It's lightweight, so it's good for hot weather.

remember: One word. 'Light' can also mean the colour.

meaning: Lets air through, so the skin stays cool.
usage: Use it for cotton and linen.

examples.sentence: Breathable cotton, perfect for summer.
The fabric is soft and breathable.

remember: Stress: BREATH-uh-bul.

meaning: A special event, such as a wedding or festival.
usage: Use it to suggest where to wear the saree.

examples.sentence: Perfect for weddings and festive occasions.
What occasion is it for?

remember: Spelling: OCCASION - two c, one s. Ask 'What is the occasion?' to guide the customer.

meaning: Suitable for festivals and celebrations.
usage: Use it for rich, bright sarees.

examples.sentence: A festive silk saree for Onam.
This one is more festive; the other is for daily wear.

remember: Festive wear, daily wear, office wear, party wear.

meaning: Simple, graceful, and stylish.
usage: Use it for a refined look.

examples.sentence: An elegant cream saree with a gold border.
It's elegant but not heavy.

remember: Do not overuse 'beautiful'. Mix with: elegant, graceful, classic, subtle.

meaning: Bright and full of colour.
usage: Use it for strong, bright shades.

examples.sentence: A vibrant red with a green border.
The colours are vibrant but not loud.

remember: Opposite: muted or soft.

meaning: Gentle and not strong or loud.
usage: Use it for quiet designs and colours.

examples.sentence: A subtle zari border.
The pattern is subtle, so it goes with anything.

remember: The 'b' is silent: SUT-l.

meaning: Silk made only from silk thread, with nothing mixed in.
usage: Use it only when 100% true.

examples.sentence: Pure silk, certified.
This is a silk-cotton blend, not pure silk.

remember: Honest labels build trust. Say 'blend' or 'silk-cotton' when mixed.

meaning: A mix of two or more fibres.
usage: Use it for mixed fabrics.

examples.sentence: A cotton-linen blend.
This blend is easier to wash than pure silk.

remember: 'Blend' is a mix. 'Pure' is only one fibre.

meaning: Do not wash at home; take it to a dry cleaner.
usage: Use it in care instructions.

examples.sentence: Care: dry clean only.
Please dry clean this one for the first wash.

remember: Short care lines are best: 'Dry clean only', 'Gentle hand wash', 'Do not bleach'.

meaning: Does not lose its colour when washed.
usage: Use it with care for strong colours.

examples.sentence: Colour-fast cotton.
Wash the first time separately, as new fabric can release some dye.

remember: Be careful: say 'colour-fast' only if you have tested it.

meaning: A ready-made blouse.
usage: Use it when you sell blouses.

examples.sentence: Stitched blouse available in sizes S to XL.
The saree comes with an unstitched blouse piece.

remember: Stitched = ready made. Unstitched = fabric only.

meaning: Extra fabric included with the saree to make a blouse.
usage: Use it to say what the customer will get.

examples.sentence: Comes with a matching blouse piece.
The blouse piece is 0.8 metres.

remember: Always mention if it is included.

meaning: Only a few pieces made.
usage: Use it to show a design is special.

examples.sentence: Limited edition: only five pieces.
This design is limited edition, so I won't restock.

remember: Use it only when it is true.

meaning: To bring back items that sold out.
usage: Use it in posts and replies.

examples.sentence: Sold-out sarees are restocking this Friday!
Would you like me to tell you when it's restocked?

remember: Verb: restock (one word). 'Back in stock' also works.
